learning_experiences: reflect and journal personal abilities and interests and share with a friend in class,
brainstorm on how to use personal abilities and interests for holistic development and make presentations in class,
share personal values that help him or her pull through as a steady person,
use print or digital resources to search for how to develop personal principles and share in class,
search using digital or print media how to manage emotions (happiness, love, fear, and anger) in day-to-day life,
share previous experiences in groups how he/she dealt with emotions,
watch relevant video clips or print media on effective management of emotions in day-to-day life.
key_inquiry_questions: How can personal abilities and interests influence career choices?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: learners reflect and journal personal abilities and interests and share them with a friend in class.
Critical Thinking and Problem-solving: learners share previous experiences in groups and how he or she dealt with emotions.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: learners brainstorm on how to use personal abilities and interests for holistic development and make presentations in class.
Responsibility: learners use print or digital resources to search for how to develop personal principles and share in class.
sub_strands.pcis: Decision-making skills: Learners reflect and journal personal abilities and interests hence and with a friend in class.
sub_strands.links: English/Kiswahili/KSL: learners use speaking and listening skills to brainstorm on personal abilities and interests for holistic development.

outcomes.text: explore personal abilities and interests for holistic development
develop personal values for a steady personality
manage emotions in day-to-day life
appreciate personal awareness in day-to-day life

learning_experiences: using digital or print media to search and classify entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies and make a presentation in class,
create posters of common entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies and display them in class,
use digital or print media to find out the personality requirements for any five social studies entrepreneurial opportunities in day-to-day life and make presentations in class,
draw charts showing an alignment of personal talents or abilities with different entrepreneurial opportunities in the country,
engage a relevant resource person to give a talk on entrepreneurial opportunities versus personality types
key_inquiry_questions: What is entrepreneurship
Which entrepreneurial opportunities exist in society?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination: learners create posters of common entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies and display them in class.
Digital Literacy: learners use digital or print resources to explore entrepreneurial opportunities in Social Studies.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learners create a poster of all entrepreneurial opportunities available in Social Studies and display it in school.
sub_strands.pcis:
Career exploration: learners draw charts aligning personal talents and abilities with available entrepreneurial opportunities.
Decision-making Skills: learners develop analytical and critical thinking skills as they use digital or print resources to explore entrepreneurial opportunities in Social Studies.
sub_strands.links: Pre-Technical Studies: learners draw charts aligning personal talents and abilities with available entrepreneurial opportunities.

learning_experiences: engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human origin from different communities,
compare the different stories on human origin from their communities and share in class,
write a collaborative essay on traditional and religious stories of human origin,
record traditional stories about the origin of humankind in society,
use relevant print or electronic media, resources to research and present in class the traditional and religious stories about the origin of humankind,
discuss ways of recording traditional stories about the origin of humankind in society.
discuss the implications of the traditional and religious stories on human origin.
key_inquiry_questions: How did human beings come to be?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and Collaboration: learners engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human origin from different communities.
sub_strands.values: Respect: learners discuss in turn the implications of the traditional and religious stories on human origin.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Awareness: learners relate with others well as they compare different stories on human origin.
sub_strands.links: Religious Education: learners relate with creation stories as they engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human origin.

outcomes.text: explore traditional stories of human origin from African communities
explain religious stories about the origin of humankind
illustrate common aspects found in traditional and religious stories of human origin
acknowledge religious and traditional stories of human origin

learning_experiences: brainstorm on factors that led to the growth of ancient Egypt, Great Zimbabwe, and the Kingdom of Kongo,
use appropriate digital or print media to find out the location of ancient Egypt, Great Zimbabwe, and the Kingdom of Kongo from the map of Africa,
watch and critique audio-visual documentary on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation,
write an essay on the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the development of the modern world civilisation and present it in class.

sub_strands.core_competences: Critical thinking: learners watch and critique audio-visual documentaries on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation.
sub_strands.values: Unity: learners watch and critique audio-visual documentaries on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation.
sub_strands.pcis: Self-esteem: learners write and present in class an essay on the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the development of modern world civilisation.
sub_strands.links: Creative Arts: learners relate the ancient contribution of Ancient to the modern world civilisation, by applying knowledge drawn from architectural designs, dressing, and artefacts.

outcomes.text: explore factors that led to the growth of the selected ancient Kingdoms in Africa
locate the selected ancient Kingdoms on a map of Africa
assess the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the modern world civilisation
appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of slavery and servitude and share their findings in class,
discuss various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society,
use digital or print resources to find out the factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade,

sub_strands.values:
Unity: learners work in groups to brainstorm on various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society.
Responsibility: learners observe safety precautions as they use print or digital resources to locate the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa.
sub_strands.pcis: Human Rights: learners identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society and locate areas where slaves were taken during the Indian Ocean slave trade,
sub_strands.links: Learners use speaking skills as they brainstorm on forms of slavery and servitude.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: lessons: table says 4, summary says 5.

outcomes.text: identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society
explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade
sketch the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa
desire to promote human dignity for a just and peaceful world

learning_experiences: discuss the comparison between barter trade and the use of currency in Africa,
use digital /print media to find out factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa,
brainstorm on the impact of the introduction of money in Africa,
engage a resource person to give a talk on the impact of the introduction of money in Africa,
role play barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa and provide a critique.
key_inquiry_questions: How has money transformed trade in Africa?

sub_strands.values: Respect: learners develop acceptance as they listen to each other as they brainstorm on the impact of the introduction of money in Africa.
sub_strands.pcis: Self-awareness: learners role play a barter trade and the use of currency.
sub_strands.links: Pre-Technical Studies: Learners apply knowledge gained from the impact of introduction of currency in Africa.

outcomes.text: compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa
trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa
deduce the impact of the introduction of money in Africa
appreciate the medium of trade for sustainability

Self-esteem: learners develop creative skills as they compose and recite poems that propagate inclusion and diversity.
Self-awareness: learners role play the personality attributes to enhance self-awareness.

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the qualities of a peaceful person in the community
write an essay on the qualities of a peaceful person
use digital or print resources to find out peaceful conflict resolution process,
engage a resource person to give a talk on factors that promote peaceful co-existence,
role play in peaceful conflict resolution process in day-to-day life,
compose and recite peace poems on the importance of peaceful co-existence in the community in day-to-day life.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we promote peace for mutual social well-being?
How can I manage stress and emotion to promote inner peace?

sub_strands.values: Peace: learners role play peaceful conflict resolution process in day-to-day life.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Cohesion: learners write down what they plan to do to improve inner peace and relationships with their family, school, or community.
sub_strands.links: Learners use creative skills to compose and recite peace poems in class.

outcomes.text: outline the qualities of a peaceful person in the community
explore factors that promote peaceful co-existence
assess peaceful conflict resolution process in day-to-day life
value the importance of peaceful coexistence in the community in day-to-day life

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of the terms community, community services, community service learning (CSL), project (activities outside class), problem (gaps or opportunities), solution (remedy), plan of activity, implementation, and written report of a project.
discuss the steps involved in carrying out a CSL project:
- identification and verification of a problem/gap/opportunity
- planning to solve an identified problem
- designing solution(s) to the problem
- implementing the solution/filling the gap
- reflecting and reporting on the project/activity done
identify and brainstorm on problems/gaps in their context/community.
discuss, verify, and adopt one problem for the class/group project.
propose and plan way(s) of solving the problem.
implement the solution to the problem in the community.
write and report on the accomplished project,
discuss CSL benefits for self and the community.
key_inquiry_questions: How can community service learning contribute to community development?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: learners develop skills of listening keenly and effectively as they discuss and brainstorm on types of projects and identification of relevant community problems.
Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learners develop the skill of exploring complex problems as they identify projects that can be undertaken in the community.
Self-efficacy: learners develop self-awareness skills as they consider the steps in a CSL project and propose ways in which they can present CSL findings.
sub_strands.values:
Love: learners develop selflessness as they engage in a discussion on the benefits of CSL for self and community.
Responsibility: learners develop self-drive as they implement the solution to the problem in the community
sub_strands.links: All subjects as they provide PCIs and undertake CSL activities.

outcomes.text: explain the meaning of key terms used in community service learning (CSL) and CSL projects
describe the importance of CSL in the community
outline steps of a CSL project/activity
execute a class CSL project
desire to conduct CSL projects in the community

learning_experiences: use appropriate print media or digital resources to identify sources of historical information in society and share in class,
design posters on primary and secondary sources of historical information in society and display them in class,
watch documentaries or video clips on the ways of preserving sources of historical information.
debate on the significance of various sources of historical information in providing evidence of past human accounts.
key_inquiry_questions: How significant are sources of historical information in understanding past human accounts?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication: learners express themselves with clarity as they debate on the significance of historical information.
Digital Literacy: learners use digital technology to effectively accomplish their tasks as they find out the sources of historical information using appropriate media.
sub_strands.values:
Patriotism: learners develop dedication as they debate on the significance of various sources of historical information in providing evidence of past human accounts.
Responsibility: learners diligently use appropriate print media or digital resources to find out sources of historical information.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Cohesion: learners debate as a class on the significance of historical sources of information in society.
sub_strands.links:
Learners apply listening and speaking skills as they discuss in small groups, sources of historical information in the society.
Learners apply creative skills as they design posters on primary and secondary sources of historical information in society.

outcomes.text: identify various sources of historical information in the society
distinguish between primary and secondary sources of historical information
explore how various sources of historical information have been preserved over the years
appreciate the significance of various sources of historical information in providing evidence of past human accounts

learning_experiences: use digital devices/ other sources to draw the map of Africa and show areas where early agriculture was practised in selected geographical regions. (Rift Valley of Eastern Africa, Egypt, and Nubia),
discuss the contribution of the Nile Valley agriculture to the world civilisation,
compose poems the importance of domestication of plants and animals in Africa.

How did Agriculture begin in Africa?

Digital Literacy: learners carry out research on the factors that favoured growing of crops and rearing of animals in selected regions during early agriculture,(in Egypt, Nubia, and in the Rift Valley of the Eastern African region and report the findings to the class,
Communication and collaboration: Learners apply listening and speaking skills as they compose poems the importance of domestication of plants and animals in Africa.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism: learners develop citizenship as they discuss the contribution of the Nile Valley agriculture to world civilisation.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Cohesion: learners discuss the contribution of the Nile Valley agriculture to the world civilisation,
sub_strands.links: Learners use knowledge of animal husbandry as they research on animals kept and types of crops which were grown during early agriculture in Egypt, Nubia and in Rift valley of the Eastern African region.

outcomes.text: locate areas where early agriculture was practised in selected geographical regions in Africa
explore factors that favoured growing of crops and rearing of animals in selected regions during early agriculture
assess the contributions of the Nile Valley agriculture to the world civilisation
value the importance of domestication of plants and animals in Africa

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the position, shape, and size of Africa and share in class,
buzz on the countries that make up Africa and display in class,
draw an outline map of Africa creatively and indicate the countries that make up Africa and display it in class,

Social Cohesion: learners brainstorm on the position, shape, and size of Africa.

sub_strands.values:
Love: learners display aspects of interconnectedness and interdependence among countries in the world today
Patriotism: learners demonstrate loyalty as they brainstorm on the qualities of a global citizen in modern society.
sub_strands.pcis:
Inter-racial-ethnic relations: learners brainstorm on the qualities of a global citizen in modern society.
Human dignity: learners debate on positive and negative effects of globalisation at local and national levels and propose solutions.
sub_strands.links: Learners apply computer skills as they use print or digital resources to research the qualities of a global citizen and write them down.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: lessons: table says 4, summary says 5.

outcomes.text: explain why there is interconnectedness and interdependence among countries in the world today
examine the effects of globalisation at national and global levels
describe the qualities of a global citizen in the modern society
create awareness of the effects of globalisation at national and global levels
identify ways of contributing to the international community while maintaining loyalty to own country
appreciate interconnectedness and interdependence among countries in the world today

indicators.indicator: Ability to explore personal abilities and interests for self-improvement.

levels.EE: Learner explores personal abilities and interests for self-improvement with examples.
levels.ME: Learner explores personal abilities and interests for self-improvement.
levels.AE: Learner explores personal abilities and interests for self-improvement omitting a few details.
levels.BE: Learner explores personal abilities and interests for self-improvement omitting many details.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality.

levels.EE: Learner identifies entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality using examples.
levels.ME: Learner identifies entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality.
levels.AE: Learner identifies entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality leaving out a few of them.
levels.BE: Learner identifies entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality leaving out many of them.

indicators.indicator: Ability to assess the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation.

levels.EE: learner assesses the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation comprehensively.
levels.ME: learner assesses the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation.
levels.AE: learner assesses the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the modern world civilisation leaving out few contributions.
levels.BE: learner assesses the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the modern world civilisation leaving out many contributions.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society.

levels.EE: Learner identifies the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society with examples.
levels.ME: Learner identifies the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society.
levels.AE: Learner identifies the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society omitting a few details.
levels.BE: Learner identifies the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society omitting many details.

indicators.indicator: Ability to locate on a map of Africa the areas settled by the three selected African communities.

levels.EE: learner locates on a map of Africa the areas settled by the three selected African communities with precision.
levels.ME: learner locates on a map of Africa the areas settled by the three selected African communities.
levels.AE: learner locates on a map of Africa the areas settled by 2 selected African communities.
levels.BE: learner locates on a map of Africa the areas settled by one or none of the selected African communities.

indicators.indicator: Ability to trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa.

levels.EE: Learner traces the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa comprehensively.
levels.ME: Learner traces the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa.
levels.AE: Learner traces the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa leaving out few factors.
levels.BE: Learner traces the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa leaving out many factors.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify different relationships in society.

levels.EE: Learner identifies different relationships in society.
levels.ME: Learner identifies different relationships in society.
levels.AE: Learner identifies different relationships in society Omitting minor details.
levels.BE: Learner identifies different relationships in society omitting major details.

indicators.indicator: Ability to explore the qualities of a peaceful person in the community.

levels.EE: Learner explores the qualities of a peaceful person in the community exhaustively.
levels.ME: Learner explores the qualities of a peaceful person in the community.
levels.AE: Learner explores the qualities of a peaceful person in the community leaving out a few qualities.
levels.BE: Learner explores the qualities of a peaceful person in the community leaving out many details.

indicators.indicator: Ability to explain the steps in a CSL project/activity.

levels.EE: Learner explains the steps in a CSL project exhaustively.
levels.ME: Learner explains the steps in a CSL project.
levels.AE: Learner explains most of the details in the CSL project.
levels.BE: Learner explains a few of the steps in the CSL project.

indicators.indicator: Ability to accomplish a CSL project/activity in group(s).

levels.EE: Learner accomplished a CSL project/activity in group(s) excellently.
levels.ME: Learner accomplished a CSL project/activity in group(s).
levels.AE: Learner did not complete the CSL project/activity in group(s).
levels.BE: Learner did not attempt the CSL project/activity in group(s).

indicators.indicator: Ability to explain the importance of CSL in the community.

levels.EE: Learner explains clearly the importance of CSL in the community.
levels.ME: Learner explains the importance of CSL in the community.
levels.AE: Learner explains fairly the importance of CSL in the community.

indicators.indicator: Ability to explore crops grown and animals kept in selected regions during early agriculture.

levels.ME: Learner explores crops grown and animals kept in selected regions during early agriculture.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe the position, shape, and size of Africa.

levels.EE: Learner describes comprehensively the position, shape, and size of Africa.
levels.ME: Learner describes the position, shape, and size of Africa.
levels.AE: Learner describes the position, shape, and size of Africa leaving fewer gaps.
levels.BE: Learner describes with major gaps the position, shape, and size of Africa.

indicators.indicator: Ability to use latitudes and longitudes to locate places and features on a map.

levels.EE: Learner uses latitudes and longitudes to locate places and features on a map excellently.
levels.ME: Learner uses latitudes and longitudes to locate places and features on a map.
levels.AE: Learner uses latitudes and longitudes to locate most places and features on a map.
levels.BE: Learner uses latitudes and longitudes to locate fewer places and features on a map.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe the origin, size, shape, and position of the earth in the solar system.

levels.EE: Learner describes the origin, size, shape, and position of the earth in the solar system with examples.
levels.ME: Learner describes the origin, size, shape, and position of the earth in the solar system.
levels.AE: Learner partially describes the origin, size, shape, and position of the earth in the solar system.
levels.BE: Learner hardly describes the origin, size, shape, and position of the earth in the solar system.

indicators.indicator: Ability to examine methods of data collection used in fieldwork, Ability to explore challenges and possible solutions in carrying out fieldwork, Ability to illustrate methods of data analysis after fieldwork

levels.EE: Examines all the methods of data collection used in fieldwork, Explores challenges and possible solutions in carrying out fieldwork using detailed examples illustrates methods of data analysis after fieldwork with detailed examples
levels.ME: Examines most of methods of data collection used in fieldwork, explores challenges and possible solutions in carrying out fieldwork using most of the examples Illustrates methods of data analysis after fieldwork with most examples
levels.AE: Examines the methods of data collection used in fieldwork,leaving out some. Explores challenges and possible solutions in carrying out fieldwork,using some examples Illustrates methods of data analysis after fieldwork while leaving out some examples
levels.BE: examines methods of data collection used in fieldwork, leaving out most. Explores challenges and possible solutions in carrying out fieldwork,using very few examples. Illustrates methods of data analysis after fieldwork while leaving most examples.

indicators.indicator: Ability to examine the political organisation of the selected African communities up to 1900. Ability to discuss the importance of the Constitution of Kenya for social well-being. Ability to analyse ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya for social cohesion.

levels.EE: Examines the political organisation of the selected African communities up to 1900 exhaustively. Discusses the importance of the Constitution of Kenya for social well-being with examples. Analyses ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya for social cohesion with examples.
levels.ME: Examines the political organisation of the selected African communities up to 1900. Discusses the importance of the Constitution of Kenya for social well-being. Analyses ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya for social cohesion.
levels.AE: Fairly examines the political organisation of the selected African communities up to 1900. Discusses the importance of the Constitution of Kenya for social well-being with minor gaps Analyses ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya for social cohesion with many few errors.
levels.BE: Hardly examines the political organisation of the selected African communities up to 1900. Discusses the importance of the Constitution of Kenya for social wellbeing with major gaps. Analyses ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya for social cohesion with many errors.

indicators.indicator: Ability to explore the characteristics of Human Rights as practised for the preservation of life. Ability to explain the concept of equity and non-discrimination in fostering solidarity. Ability to explore the factors that contributed to the presence of African diasporas across the world.

levels.EE: Explores the characteristics of Human Rights as practised for the preservation of life exhaustively. Explains the concept of equity and non-discrimination in fostering solidarity elaborately. Explores the factors which contributed to the presence of African diasporas across the world comprehensively.
levels.ME: Explores the characteristics of Human Rights as practised for the preservation of life. Explains the concept of equity and non-discrimination in fostering solidarity. Explores the factors which contributed to the presence of African diasporas across the world.
levels.AE: Explores some characteristics of Human Rights as practised for the preservation of life. Explains one of the concepts of equity and non-discrimination in fostering solidarity. Explores more than half of the factors that contributed to the presence of African diasporas across the world.
levels.BE: Explores some characteristics of Human Rights as practised for the preservation of life. Explains the concept of equity and non-discrimination in fostering solidarity with support. Explores less than half of the factors that contributed to the presence of African diasporas across the world.

indicators.indicator: Ability to assess the role of the diaspora in the political development in Africa. Ability to explain the interconnectedness and interdependence of different countries. Ability to describe qualities of a global citizen in modern society.

levels.EE: Assesses the role of the diaspora in the political development in Africa exhaustively. Explains the interconnectedness and interdependence of different countries with examples. Describes the qualities of a global citizen in modern society with examples.
levels.ME: Assesses the role of the diaspora in the political development in Africa. Explains the interconnectedness and interdependence of different countries. Describes qualities of a global citizen in modern society.
levels.AE: Partly assesses the role of the diaspora in the political development in Africa partially. Explains the interconnectedness and interdependence of different countries partially. Describes some qualities of a global citizen in modern society.
levels.BE: Hardly assesses the role of the diaspora in the political development in Africa. Explains the interconnectedness and interdependence of different countries with support. Describes qualities of a global citizen in modern society with assistance.
